question_images.label: Figure 2
question_images.description: Reaction scheme showing the ring-opening substitution of a cyclopropylmethanol derivative. Two diastereomers of the starting material (differing at the CH(OH)R3 stereocenter) both react with HBF4 and CuBr2 to give the same homoallylic fluoride product with an (E)-double bond and specific stereochemistry at the newly formed C-F center.

question_images.label: Figure 3
question_images.description: Reaction scheme showing the stereospecific SN1 reaction of a homoallylic alcohol. The starting material HO-CH(R3)-C(R1)(R2)-CH=C(R4)(R5) undergoes rearrangement upon reaction with TMSX/FeCl3 or F3S-NEt2 to form homoallylic halides X-C(R1)(R2)-CH(R3)-CH=C(R4)(R5) (where X = Cl, Br, or F) with retention of the double bond configuration and specific stereochemistry.

question_images.label: Figure 4
question_images.description: Chemical structure of Product C, a bis-indole derivative. It consists of a 5-methoxy-3-(2-(alkylamino)ethyl)-1H-indol-2-yl group attached to the C3 position of a 3-(2-(alkylamino)ethyl)-indolin-2-one group. The C3 position of the oxindole is a quaternary stereocenter with a wedge bond to the indole and a dash bond to the -CH2CH2NHR group.
